plugin.cbc.title: CBC mode (cipher block chaining)
plugin.cbc.preset.repeated-blocks: Two equal plaintext blocks: CBC hides the repetition
plugin.cbc.preset.repeated-blocks-decryp: Decrypt the two-block message and remove its padding
plugin.cbc.param.cipherHint: The block cipher E_K that CBC calls once per block.
plugin.cbc.param.keyHint: A key the block cipher accepts, e.g. 16, 24 or 32 bytes for AES.
plugin.cbc.param.ivHint: One block (16 bytes for AES). It must be unpredictable for every message.
plugin.cbc.param.inputHint: Up to 64 bytes: the plaintext to encrypt or the ciphertext to decrypt.
plugin.cbc.param.paddingHint: PKCS#7 fills the last block up; without padding the input must be whole blocks.
plugin.cbc.op.xorChain: XOR with the previous ciphertext block (or the IV)
plugin.cbc.op.emit: Emit the block and pass the chaining value on
plugin.cbc.step.initialEncrypt: The plaintext has {{bytes}} bytes. CBC encrypts it in blocks of {{blockSize}} bytes with {{cipher}}, and chains them: before encryption, each plaintext block is XORed with the previous ciphertext block, the first one with the IV.
plugin.cbc.step.initialDecrypt_one: The ciphertext has {{bytes}} bytes in one block. CBC decrypts it with {{cipher}} and then XORs the result with the IV.
plugin.cbc.step.initialDecrypt_other: The ciphertext has {{bytes}} bytes in {{count}} blocks. CBC decrypts each block with {{cipher}} and then XORs the result with the previous ciphertext block, the first one with the IV.
plugin.cbc.step.pad: PKCS#7 padding: {{count}} bytes of value {{byte}} fill the input up to {{length}} bytes, a whole number of blocks. Even an input that already fills its blocks gets a full block of padding, so the receiver can always remove it.
plugin.cbc.step.xorChainFirst: Block {{n}}: P{{n}} ⊕ IV = {{block}} ⊕ {{previous}} = {{result}}. The IV makes the first block depend on an unpredictable value.
plugin.cbc.step.xorChain: Block {{n}}: P{{n}} ⊕ C{{prev}} = {{block}} ⊕ {{previous}} = {{result}}. Through the chaining, equal plaintext blocks give different cipher inputs.
plugin.cbc.step.encryptBlock: Block {{n}}: {{cipher}} encrypts {{input}} to {{output}}. Here E_K is one opaque step; open the block cipher's lab to see its rounds.
plugin.cbc.step.emitEncrypt: C{{n}} = {{block}} goes out and becomes the chaining value for the next block.
plugin.cbc.step.decryptBlock: Block {{n}}: {{cipher}} decrypts C{{n}} = {{input}} to {{output}}. That is not P{{n}} yet: it is still XORed with the previous ciphertext block.
plugin.cbc.step.xorChainDecrypt: Block {{n}}: D_K(C{{n}}) ⊕ C{{prev}} = {{block}} ⊕ {{previous}} = {{result}}. A flipped bit in C{{prev}} flips the same bit here.
plugin.cbc.step.emitDecrypt: P{{n}} = {{block}}. The ciphertext block C{{n}} becomes the chaining value for the next block.
plugin.cbc.step.unpad: The last byte is {{byte}}, and the last {{count}} bytes all have that value: the padding is valid. Removing it leaves {{length}} bytes of plaintext.
plugin.cbc.step.unpadInvalid.empty: There is no data, so there is no padding to remove.
plugin.cbc.step.unpadInvalid.not-block-a: The data is not a whole number of blocks, so the padding is invalid.
plugin.cbc.step.unpadInvalid.zero-pad-by: The last byte is 00, but PKCS#7 never pads with zero bytes: the padding is invalid. The output keeps all decrypted blocks.
plugin.cbc.step.unpadInvalid.pad-too-lon: The last byte is {{byte}}, which claims more padding than one block of {{blockSize}} bytes holds: the padding is invalid. The output keeps all decrypted blocks.
plugin.cbc.step.unpadInvalid.inconsisten: The last byte {{byte}} claims that many padding bytes, but byte {{index}} is {{found}}: the padding is invalid. The output keeps all decrypted blocks.
plugin.cbc.error.invalidParams: Give the key, the IV and the input as hex text.
plugin.cbc.error.keyLength: The key has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 64.
plugin.cbc.error.ivLength: The IV has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 32.
plugin.cbc.error.inputLength: The input has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 64.
plugin.cbc.error.ivBlockSize: The IV has {{length}} bytes; this block cipher needs exactly {{blockSize}}.
plugin.cbc.error.notAligned: The input has {{length}} bytes, which is not a multiple of the block size {{blockSize}}. Decrypting, or encrypting without padding, needs whole blocks.
